response.query: Which quasi-experimental or longitudinal designs (stepped-wedge, interrupted time series, cohort) are most feasible and informative across our target countries and sectors?
response.answer: Stepped-wedge, interrupted time series, and cohort designs are feasible and informative for quasi-experimental and longitudinal studies across various countries and sectors. Stepped-wedge designs are particularly useful for implementation research.

results.title: Reporting of stepped wedge cluster randomised trials
results.content: The CONSORT (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials) statement, initially published in 1996 and updated in 2001 and 2010, outlines essential items to be reported in a parallel arm individually randomised trial.123 The CONSORT extension for cluster randomised trials (CRTs), initially published in 2004 and updated in 2012, extended this guidance for trials in which groups of individuals (clusters, see table 1 for a full glossary of terms) are randomised to different treatment conditions.45 In recent years, a novel type of cluster randomised design—stepped wedge cluster randomised trial (SW-CRT)—has become increasingly popular.678 The SW-CRT involves randomisation of clusters to different sequences. *Extension for SW-CRTs*—Description and diagram of trial design including definition of cluster, number of sequences, number of clusters randomised to each sequence, number of periods, duration of time between each step, and whether the participants assessed in different periods are the same people, different people, or a mixture.
